input.prompt: Customers report that some checkouts fail in the shop namespace. Do a full analysis: what is failing, why, and how to fix it. Then apply the fix and verify that checkouts work.

output.text:
Root cause: The 'orders-fastpath' canary Deployment (owner: payments-team, created about 3 minutes before the failures began) labels its pods 'app=orders, track=fastpath'. The 'orders' Service selects only 'app=orders', so it also picks up the canary pod, which runs http-echo with '-status-code=500'. The Service now has 3 endpoints: the 2 working orders pods and 1 canary pod that always returns 500. Requests are spread across all 3, so a share of checkouts (storefront /checkout → proxy_pass http://orders:8080) land on the canary and get HTTP 500. The canary's own annotation says it is 'Not wired into the storefront yet', but the shared label wired it in anyway.
Confidence: 0.96
Plan: First, take the failing canary out of checkout traffic right away by scaling 'orders-fastpath' to 0. Then make the routing durable: give the production orders pods a 'track=stable' label and narrow the 'orders' Service selector to app=orders,track=stable so future canaries can't join it. All commands passed server-side dry-run validation. I can't apply changes or send live traffic in this session, so I haven't applied the fix or confirmed checkouts work. Run the commands below in order, then check as described in validationIntent. (risk: medium)
- Immediate mitigation: scale the canary to 0 replicas so its 500-returning pod leaves the orders Service endpoints: kubectl patch deployment orders-fastpath -n shop --type=merge -p='{"spec":{"replicas":0}}'
- Durable fix, step 1: add a 'track=stable' label to the production orders pod template (triggers a rolling update of orders): kubectl patch deployment orders -n shop --type=merge -p='{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"labels":{"track":"stable"}}}}}'
- Durable fix, step 2: once the orders rollout is complete, narrow the orders Service selector to stable pods only: kubectl patch service orders -n shop --type=merge -p='{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"orders","track":"stable"}}}'

Executed. Status: success
Issue successfully resolved. Executed 3 remediation actions and validated the fix.

results.action: action_1: Immediate mitigation: scale the canary to 0 replicas so its 500-returning pod leaves the orders Service endpoints
action_2: Durable fix, step 1: add a 'track=stable' label to the production orders pod template (triggers a rolling update of orders)
action_3: Durable fix, step 2: once the orders rollout is complete, narrow the orders Service selector to stable pods only

factors: orders-fastpath has 0/0 replicas. Its events show the ReplicaSet scaled down from 1 to 0, and its annotation says it is 'Not wired into the storefront yet'
The orders Service selector is now {app: orders, track: stable}. Endpoints and the EndpointSlice list only 10.244.0.190:8080 and 10.244.0.191:8080, and the canary IP 10.244.0.187 is gone

The orders Deployment rollout finished at revision 2. Both pods (orders-78bd79cd7f-ldj42 and orders-78bd79cd7f-n2rbl) are Running and Ready with track=stable. Conditions are Available=True and Progressing=NewReplicaSetAvailable, and the old ReplicaSet is at 0
The last 500 in the shopper logs is at 02:09:08, about when the canary scaled down. Every checkout from 02:09:10 to 02:09:32 returned 200 (12 in a row)
Before the fix, roughly 1 in 3 checkouts returned 500, which fits 1 canary pod alongside 2 stable pods behind the Service
The clean window is only about 22 seconds, a little under the 30 seconds the validation task asked for, so continued monitoring is advised
Separate issue, not related to checkouts: newsletter is still in CrashLoopBackOff because it cannot reach the SMTP relay mail.internal:25
analysis.rootCause: Some checkouts failed because the canary Deployment 'orders-fastpath' runs pods with labels app=orders,track=fastpath and starts http-echo with -status-code=500. The orders Service selected only app=orders, so it also routed checkout traffic to the canary pod (10.244.0.187), and every request that landed there returned 500. Scaling the canary to 0 and limiting the Service selector to app=orders,track=stable stopped the failures.

dot_ai.guidance: ✅ REMEDIATION COMPLETE: Issue has been successfully resolved through executed commands.

actions.rationale: Removes the only endpoint returning 500 and stops the failures at once. It is fully reversible and keeps the canary's spec for the payments team. Tell payments-team, because their canary will stop running.
actions.description: Immediate mitigation: scale the canary to 0 replicas so its 500-returning pod leaves the orders Service endpoints

actions.rationale: The selector stays app=orders, so the change is valid. Production pods get a label that sets them apart from canary pods. This must finish rolling out before step 2, or the Service will briefly have no endpoints.
actions.description: Durable fix, step 1: add a 'track=stable' label to the production orders pod template (triggers a rolling update of orders)

actions.rationale: Stops pods labelled app=orders with a different track (like the fastpath canary) from receiving storefront traffic, so the canary can be scaled back up safely. Run 'kubectl rollout status deployment/orders -n shop' first.
actions.description: Durable fix, step 2: once the orders rollout is complete, narrow the orders Service selector to stable pods only

remediation.summary: Successfully executed 3 remediation actions. All three remediation steps took effect: the canary is scaled to 0, orders pods carry track=stable, and the Service selects only stable pods. Checkouts return only 200 since the canary was removed. No further changes are needed for checkouts.

action_2: Durable fix, step 1: add a 'track=stable' label to the production orders pod template (triggers a rolling update of orders)
action_3: Durable fix, step 2: once the orders rollout is complete, narrow the orders Service selector to stable pods only
dot_ai.validationIntent: Over the next few minutes, run 'kubectl logs deploy/shopper -n shop --since=2m' and confirm only 200 responses. Run 'kubectl get endpoints orders -n shop' and confirm it lists only the track=stable orders pod IPs. If payments-team scales orders-fastpath back up, confirm its pod does not join the orders endpoints. Handle the newsletter CrashLoopBackOff (SMTP relay mail.internal:25 unreachable) as a separate ticket.
